item.nyctocosm.catechism.author: The Archmage
item.nyctocosm.catechism.title: Precept %s: %s
item.nyctocosm.catechism.1.title: On Souls
item.nyctocosm.catechism.1.page1:
That soul which ends not is not.

For a soul contains itself, and nothing else. A being that is is a soul, and a being that is not has not a soul.

A soul is fluid, a soul is without edges, a soul is powerful, a soul is extant. Let us
item.nyctocosm.catechism.1.page2:
pour out the power of the soul, and rend it to our uses.

Let us weave, bind, and coalesce the power of a soul so that it does the work of purpose.

For a soul without purpose is lost, and a lost soul is rootless.
item.nyctocosm.catechism.2.title: Phosphene
item.nyctocosm.catechism.2.page1:
The world is a web. The world is a net. The world is a nest of unkempt noetic thread-twigs.

We are to bind and weave, direct and conduct. What is real and what is not? That is the decision of the Mystic.
item.nyctocosm.catechism.2.page2: The Mystic wields a needle. It is more real than reality. With it, he may pierce the folds of space and pleach the seams of time. Parting the causal waves, the Mystic opens an eye in the pervading Storm of the Cosmos.
item.nyctocosm.catechism.2.page3:
The Storm is all-encompassing, fusing thought and matter. Only in an eye can she master both, and push them apart. Only in an eye will limitless thought transmute to perceptible tangibility.

This is the power of the Mystic.
item.nyctocosm.journal.author: The Researcher
item.nyctocosm.journal.title: Log %s: %s
item.nyctocosm.journal.1.title: Ingress
item.nyctocosm.journal.1.page1:
I was sure I was dead. But no myths portrayed the afterlife as so barren, so rocky, so desolate. At least, none that I had ever heard of.
Did I dare believe in the impossible? That, in all improbability, the §kGATEWAY§r had actually fulfilled its purpose? That our years, our
item.nyctocosm.journal.1.page2:
decades of toil and travail had at last yielded success?
Despite the circumstances, I allowed myself a moment of quiet, lonely joy. We had done it. The Night Realm was in our grasp.
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.title: Préliminaire
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.page1:
§nRemark One:§r The Night Realm is dark. Its sky is faded and dull. A sun-like object gyrates and pulses violently, searing twin scars of light across the void.

§nRemark Two:§r The Night Realm is dead. The growths sprinkled about the nightscape are petrified corpses,
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.page2:
remnants and shadows of what once was.

§nRemark Three:§r The resonant growth we have dubbed "Sculk" that had so ravenously enveloped our dimensional breaches seems to be diminished here. My theories seem to be correct: Sculk emerges at the
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.page3:
boundaries of dimensions and is not native to the Night Realm itself.

§nRemark Four:§r The Night Realm is broken. Our projections converge on a Telic Immaculus. A vivid world unantagonized is rigorously proven to reach evolutionary perfection, not death.
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.page4:
Thus, the state of the Night Realm leaves some unanswered questions:

Who used to live here? What happened? And, what §owill§r happen?
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.title: Tenebrity
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page1:
I could not see. I could not hear, could not breathe, could not think, could not...
I apologize. I have not fully recovered. Rationality yet eludes my fractured mind.

I did not anticipate the effect this place would have on my psyche. I believe myself strong-willed,
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page2:
but I lost the entirety of my rational faculties in the episode I just experienced.

I had been testing the heft of some geological samples collected from the land. Without warning, I lost my sense of sight, and severe
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page3:
hallucinations followed. I could hear my heart pounding, louder than I have ever heard before. An excruciating sense of fear, of dread, of §oimpending doom§r washed over me and I could feel nothing else. I did not know what to do.

In my panic, I looked up at the sky, at the
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page4:
pulsing, whirling star above. The faint starlight allowed my mind to surface briefly, and I realized I was being starved of light.

I managed to draw my fire-starting tools, striking a few sparks into a flame. Immediately, my sanity returned and I could
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page5:
think clearly again. We often take light for granted. Little do we realize how distraught and lost we would be without it.

I wonder: does some unknown property of this dimension amplify the effects of darkness upon the psyche? Whatever it is,
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page6: I have learned my lesson. I will not stray from the light.
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.title: Obduracy
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page1:
Imagine a great tree, rooted in the loam of time. The waves of entropy push and pull against its trunk, all to no avail. Violent winds of chance and change buffet its leaves, but it stands strong and does not waver.

Now imagine another, smaller tree. This one
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page2:
has shallow, weak roots. Mercilessly bombarded on all sides by winds and water, the tree is uprooted and carried away into eternity, never to be seen again. All traces of its existence are erased.

My research has led me to the study of existence, of
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page3:
causal supremacy, of the teleology of all things. There are some things like the great tree; mighty and unyielding, unable to be removed. Their existences remain static, constant.
Other things are more akin to the smaller tree; pliable, deferential, easily toppled.
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page4:
These things have weak existences, and are quickly dissipated into the abyss with the gentlest of pushes.

I propose a teleological property I will call "obduracy." An obdurate object will be resistant to causal threats.
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page5:
I am not sure how an object would achieve high levels of obduracy. Perhaps it would require interactions with a higher plane of reality? One more... §oreal§r than this one?

I will have to do more research. From my encounters with the §kGUARDIAN§r,
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page6: I fear it may be necessary in the future.

item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.title: Theorem %s: %s
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.author: Tarph-Xolaeta
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.lore: An ancient, fragmented textbook covered in handwritten notes
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.1.title: Introduction
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.1.page1: Axiotopology is our word for the study of semiaxiomatic hyperphenomena as related to the underlying topology of the "flow" of causality in our universe. With a strong understanding of axiotopology, one will be able to construct semiaxioms to resolve problems
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.1.page2: such as the Reverse-Homology Causal Reduction Problem, the Chirality Problem for Entropy, and the Post-Flow Decision Matrix Parsing Problem, to name a few. Solving these problems is one of the first and foremost steps to manifesting
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.2.title: Semiaxiomatic Fields and Standard Topology
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.2.page1.part: Perhaps the most fundamental process involved in hyperphenomenal manifestation is the construction of a localized

§6§lDefinition §f§n§oSemiaxiomatic Field

§r§7A free, finite volume of reduced or augmented
semiaxiomatic energy enclosed in a topologically
isomorphic region of spacetime.

(SAF).

The construction of a SAF is essential in any attempt to manifest hyperphenomena. This is because
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.2.page2.part: hyperphenomena cannot occur within the closures of

§6§lDefinition §f§n§oStandard Topology

§r§7The pervading semiaxiomatic energy level
of the universe. Defined conventionally as
0Þ.

.

By generating a SAF, one may then prescribe superstandard behaviors to local spacetime. These behaviors, once realized, can then propagate out from
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.2.page3:
within the SAF to the exterior Standard Topological spacetime. This process is called transmutation.

Theoretically, it is possible to generate infinitely expanding SAF that disseminate at the maximum speed of Standard Topology. However, this would be an irreversible
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.2.page4: process and will eventually erase all of Standard Topology, replacing it with a new topology based on the energy levels present in the SAF. However, this is unlikely to occur due to the extreme magnitudes of semiaxiomatic potential required to catalyze such an event.
